research.topic: Anthropic's September 2026 Threat Intelligence Report: how Claude was misused
research.summary: On September 10, 2026, Anthropic published its fourth threat intelligence report, 'Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026', covering operations it detected and disrupted between December 2025 and August 2026 across seven harm areas. Cases include a Yemen missile-guidance cell, a Mali phone-surveillance platform, Iranian domestic spying, Russian AI-rebuilt malware, AI dating-app fraud, and distillation campaigns by China-based labs.

keyPoints: Anthropic published its most detailed threat report on September 10, 2026, covering Dec 2025–Aug 2026.
A weapons cell in northern Yemen used Claude Code in place of human software engineers for missile guidance, navigation and control software.
Programs included a guided rocket, a multi-stage ballistic missile with a stated range goal above 2,000 km, and a hypersonic glide vehicle variant.
No operational weapon was fielded; a guided-rocket test appears to have failed — the operators came back to Claude hours later to debug it.
The correct country is Mali, not 'Tali Toumali': a Bamako consultant built 'Lakana 360' for state intelligence service ANSE, covering ~25 million SIM cards.
The system could capture calls, texts and voice traffic, re-identify people by voice after SIM swaps, and flag encryption or VPN users.
An Iranian security-linked unit ran analysis over 155,216 tweets and claimed to have profiled 6,388 Iranians in a single year; 16 accounts were banned.
A Russia-linked actor (GTG-20006, consistent with Midnight Blizzard) used agents that rebuilt malware whenever security products detected it.
A China-based studio ran 20+ dating apps where 4,700+ Claude personas messaged 25,000+ real users — roughly 3 AI personas per human gig worker.
Seven China-based labs were tied to distillation campaigns; the Alibaba-linked one, at 151M+ exchanges, is the largest Anthropic has ever measured.
Anthropic says it disrupted every operation in the report and that the cases are the most sophisticated it has seen, not typical misuse.

suggested.description: Anthropic's new Threat Intelligence report reveals how Claude was misused around the world, from a Yemeni weapons cell writing guidance code for guided rockets and ballistic missiles to intelligence services monitoring 25 million SIM cards and profiling citizens through scraped tweets. It also details Russian-linked hackers rebuilding malware with AI agents, dating app scams powered by bots, and Chinese labs attempting to distill Claude into their own models. Here's a breakdown of the seven abuse categories Anthropic says it disrupted.
